summary.title: Threat Modeling (OWASP Community Page)
summary.one_liner: Threat modeling is a continuous, structured process for identifying threats to an application, deciding countermeasures, and checking the result, guided by the four-question framework.
keywords: what can go wrong threat analysis
takeaways: A threat model is a structured view of an application's security, including its subject, assumptions, threats, mitigations, and validation.
Threat modeling should run continuously across the lifecycle, starting at a high level early on and refining as details are added.
The four-question framework: what are we working on, what can go wrong, what are we going to do about it, and did we do a good job.
Techniques named for identifying threats include brainstorming, STRIDE, kill chains, and attack trees.
Threat models should be updated after new features, security incidents, or architectural/infrastructure changes.
summary.summary: This OWASP community page explains threat modeling as a family of activities for finding threats and defining countermeasures for software, systems, and business processes. It describes what a threat model contains and how it fits into the development lifecycle, recommending repeated updates after new features, incidents, or architecture changes. It presents a four-question framework for organizing the work and names STRIDE, kill chains, and attack trees as possible techniques. It also mentions the 2020 Threat Modeling Manifesto and the benefits of an assurance argument, and links to a separate page on a structured threat modeling process.
